name: Banh tieu
summary: Bánh tiêu is fried wheat dough with mashed steamed mung bean, eaten hot in the hand. Vietnam Tourism says the stalls show up on ordinary streets and in small lanes in Vung Tau. No street is named. A price is check on arrival.
origin: Vung Tau, on the Vietnam Tourism page that lists the local snacks.
culture: Vietnam Tourism places the stalls on ordinary streets and in small lanes, as a snack while you walk, not as a sit-down bowl.
texture: Fried wheat dough, with mashed steamed mung bean inside. Eat it hot, in the hand.
taste: The page names the dough and the steamed mung bean. It does not add a sauce or a chili. Leave the flavor at those two things.
howToEat: Eat it hot, in the hand, while you are walking.
A lane is not named. If you cannot see the dough frying, you are in the wrong place for this page.
A stall price is check on arrival.
where: Small lanes and ordinary streets. Vietnam Tourism does not name one street. Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Banh tieu in Vung Tau — fried dough, mung bean
seoDescription: Bánh tiêu is fried wheat dough with mashed steamed mung bean, sold from stalls in ordinary lanes. Eat it hot. No street is named, and a price is check on arrival.
